baselines.description: Deep-tracked legacy baseline used for the ETAX review.
Released before several July-September 2026 hardening changes.

baselines.label: Current main
baselines.description: Upstream development state at the 2026-09-18 snapshot.

components.issue: CVE-2025-34336 public advisory covers common-components up to 4.3.1. The upload surface is present in stock 3.9.0. Current upstream uses POST, but controller-local authentication is not sufficient evidence by itself to declare all deployments fixed.
components.vulnerableSignature: Upload endpoints reachable without an effective authentication/authorization boundary.
components.fixedSignature: URL security + authenticated request enforcement + POST + safe upload policy.
components.verify: Unauthenticated request should be rejected (401/403/login redirect/404). Confirm Spring Security URL rules as well as controller code.
components.evidence: CVE-2025-34336; v3.9.0 source; current upstream source

components.issue: Stock 3.9.0 decrypts path/physical/contentType and historically falls back to the original input on decrypt failure. CVE-2025-34337 describes an encryption-oracle/access-control chain around this design.
components.vulnerableSignature: decrypt() returns original input on failure; path checks rely on string filtering such as '..'.
components.fixedSignature: egovAssertLoginUser(); fail-closed decrypt; Paths.normalize(); resolvedPath.startsWith(uploadRoot); exact extension allowlist.
components.verify: Unauthenticated access must fail. Decrypt failure must not continue with plaintext. Resolved path must stay inside the upload root.
components.evidence: CVE-2025-34337; v3.9.0 vs current source diff

components.issue: Stock 3.9.0 accepts atchFileId/fileSn directly. v5.0.3 adds encrypted file-id/session binding, while later July 2026 hardening adds explicit authentication, file-id binding and safe inline MIME handling.
components.vulnerableSignature: Direct file identifiers with insufficient caller/session/object binding.
components.fixedSignature: isAuthenticated(); encrypted atchFileId/session validation; fileSn-to-atchFileId binding; safe image extension allowlist; nosniff.
components.verify: Unauthenticated requests and cross-session/cross-object identifiers must be rejected; unsafe extensions must download as attachment.
components.evidence: v3.9.0, v5.0.3 and current main source comparison; NCSC/NIA patch wave

components.issue: Stock 3.9.0 checks only that a caller is authenticated on write paths while the scheduler/checker executes the stored ceckSql. Current main adds @RequireAdmin to registration/update/delete paths, but the SQL execution capability itself remains by design.
components.vulnerableSignature: Authenticated non-admin can register/update monitoring SQL or reach equivalent functionality.
components.fixedSignature: @RequireAdmin on sensitive management paths plus runtime access-control enforcement.
components.verify: Use a normal user and administrator in staging. Non-admin users must not register/update/delete DB monitor definitions or schedule SQL execution.
components.upstreamState: Authorization hardened; capability still requires runtime review
components.evidence: v3.9.0 vs current controller; Project Canopy/SK shieldus public description

components.issue: The 2023 official security patch labels the function as a development/test function with a security weakness and comments out the handler/service path.
components.vulnerableSignature: Active sitemap creation endpoint calling creatSiteMap()/siteMapCreat().
components.fixedSignature: Function disabled/removed in upstream security patch.
components.verify: Search for the endpoint and active service call. If customized equivalent functionality remains, review file-write paths and authorization.

components.issue: Stock 3.9.0 builds a File directly from the submitted batchProgrm after blacklist filtering. The 2023 patch constrains it under SHELL.batchShellFolder.
components.verify: Confirm the component is used and batch program paths cannot escape the approved batch shell directory.

components.issue: Later security patches sanitize filesystem names before passing them to FileSystemChecker, removing CRLF and command-separator-like characters.
components.vulnerableSignature: Raw fileSysNm reaches filesystem checker / scheduling logic.
components.verify: Confirm the feature exists and user-controlled filesystem names are constrained before any OS/filesystem utility use.

components.issue: The 2025 security patch introduces explicit approved-root validation and changes FileTool APIs to include/validate a base path.
components.vulnerableSignature: File operations derive paths without an approved-root validator.
components.verify: Trace all callers of FileTool methods and confirm effective canonical/root containment, including customized wrappers.

components.issue: Stock 3.9.0 exposes getFileName(String filePath) and concatenates configurable paths/file names. The 2025 patch fixes the local root to Globals.SynchrnServerPath and later hardening normalizes names.
components.vulnerableSignature: Caller-controlled filePath or filename concatenation reaches local file operations.
components.fixedSignature: Fixed SYNCH_SERVER_PATH root; filename basename/allow-list checks.
components.verify: Confirm all upload/list/delete/download operations are confined to the intended sync directory.

components.featureAnchor: Controllers with state changes + Spring Security CSRF configuration
components.issue: Project Canopy and later NCSC patch waves identified large numbers of state-changing handlers that needed POST restrictions and CSRF-aware form changes. POST-only is necessary but not sufficient for session-cookie applications.
components.vulnerableSignature: State-changing action accepts GET and/or POST without effective CSRF validation.
components.fixedSignature: Safe HTTP method + CSRF enabled + valid token required for state-changing session-authenticated requests.
components.verify: GET should fail for state changes; POST without/with invalid CSRF token should fail; valid token should succeed.
components.upstreamState: Broad hardening; deployment-specific verification still required
components.evidence: Project Canopy report; PR #1140 inventory; NCSC patch waves

components.featureAnchor: Multiple BBS, schedule, survey, trouble-request, comment and user-facing controllers
components.issue: Object-level authorization fixes continued through September 2026, including schedule, satisfaction and trouble-request paths. This means a release version alone is not a complete proof of coverage.
components.vulnerableSignature: Object identifier from request is trusted without owner/admin authorization against the loaded object.
components.fixedSignature: Load object first; compare owner/registrant to authenticated user or enforce admin role; reject mismatch.
components.verify: Two-account regression: user B must not read/update/delete user A's objects, attachments, schedules, comments or private records.

components.featureAnchor: @RequireAdmin and equivalent role checks across management controllers
components.issue: @RequireAdmin was introduced in the 5.0.2 patch set, but additional admin restrictions were still being added in August and September 2026.
components.vulnerableSignature: Sensitive management path checks only login status or trusts UI/menu exposure as an authorization boundary.
components.fixedSignature: Server-side admin role enforcement on every sensitive read/write management operation.
components.verify: Enumerate admin functions and test with an authenticated non-admin account. Do not rely on hidden menus or URL obscurity.
components.evidence: 5.0.2 patch, NCSC/NIA patch, Sep 17 admin commits

components.issue: The eGovFrame runtime v3.9.0 logging module declares log4j-core 2.11.2, which is in the affected Log4Shell range if that JAR is actually deployed.
components.vulnerableSignature: WEB-INF/lib/log4j-core-2.11.2.jar (or another affected log4j-core release) in the deployed WAR.
components.fixedSignature: Supported non-vulnerable Log4j release and verified deployed dependency graph/SBOM.
components.verify: Inspect the deployed WAR, not only source pom.xml. Presence of log4j-api alone is not equivalent to log4j-core exposure.
components.upstreamState: Dependency must be verified in the actual artifact
components.evidence: eGovFrame runtime v3.9.0 pom + Apache Log4j security advisory
